newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower on sagging UBS.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower on sagging UBS.

text.p: Swiss shares closed lower on sagging UBS shares, which slid three percent following the bank's announcement one-off extraordinary provisions of three billion Swiss francs would lead to a net loss of around 500 million francs in 1996.
Prices were also pressured by transactions linked to derivative trading, dealers said. Most traders voiced disappointment with the market's sluggish performance despite record levels on Wall Street.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) gave up 13.8 points, or 0.35 percent, to 3,877.9 points.
All-share SPI fell 8.44 points to 2,476.96 points.
UBS bearer shares led the actives list, slumping 41 francs or 3.23 percent to 1,229 francs. Dealers said speculative hopes for dramatic news did not materialise from a UBS news conference.
UBS restructuring plans for domestic business offered few surprises and there were no concrete statements about the sale of UBS' stake in Motor Columbus, they added.
Financials were negatively affected by UBS' slide. Insurer Swiss Re added seven francs to 1,449 ahead of the pay-out of a dividend on Wednesday.
Industrials showed mostly little reaction to the U.S. dollar's firmer tone.
Watchmaker SMH, Ciba registered shares, Electrowatt and Nestle posted gains.
ABB, Roche, Sandoz and Sulzer were lower. Roche certificates fell below 10,000 francs, ending 40 francs down at 9,970.
Motor Columbus stocks ended flat at 2,680. Some dealers regretted there were no clear statements from UBS's news conference about a possible sale of UBS's majority sale in Motor Columbus.
